title: D-FINE-L vs RT-DETR-R50m: benchmark on protocol
dek: Measured on the same COCO protocol: D-FINE-L leads by 6.2 mAP points, but RT-DETR-R50m is 38% faster on desktop GPU and that lead vanishes on a Raspberry Pi 5.
author: Vision Analysis

blocks.text: D-FINE-L is the more accurate detector: 60.0 vs 53.8 mAP@50-95 against RT-DETR-R50m on an RTX 5070 Ti in PyTorch, a 6.2-point lead. RT-DETR-R50m answers with speed, running 38% faster at 35.3 vs 21.9 FPS. D-FINE-L also holds the smaller memory footprint at 245 vs 302 MB peak VRAM. The speed order does not hold on Raspberry Pi 5, so pick by deployment target.

D-FINE-L (31.24M parameters, Apache-2.0) and RT-DETR-R50m (36.59M, Apache-2.0) are both transformer detectors evaluated at 640 px input on COCO val2017. Both have verified rows on desktop GPU, Jetson Orin, A100, and Raspberry Pi 5, so this comparison covers the targets where the answer changes.

blocks.caption: Accuracy vs parameters on COCO val2017. D-FINE-L and RT-DETR-R50m highlighted against the full set of measured models.

blocks.text: mAP is shown in percent form. D-FINE-L measures 60.0 mAP@50-95 to RT-DETR-R50m's 53.8, and the gap is stable across runtimes. The largest single difference is on small objects: 45.9 vs 37.6 mAP_small, a 22.11% relative gap. If your scenes are dominated by small instances, that row decides the comparison.

On the RTX 5070 Ti, RT-DETR-R50m is 38.03% faster in PyTorch (35.3 vs 21.9 FPS) and the gap holds under conversion: 76.4 vs 50.9 FPS on ONNX Runtime, 102.8 vs 72.3 FPS on TensorRT FP32. On Jetson Orin the two are close: 5.0 vs 4.7 FPS.
The speed verdict does not travel to CPU. On Raspberry Pi 5 both models run at 0.4 FPS, so RT-DETR-R50m's desktop speed lead disappears. If your target is a bare Pi, the accuracy gap is what remains.

Pick D-FINE-L when accuracy leads the requirement, especially on small objects, and when peak VRAM matters at 245 vs 302 MB. Pick RT-DETR-R50m for desktop or server GPU throughput, where it runs 38.03% faster. Both ship under Apache-2.0, so licensing does not force the choice.

# pip install libreyolo
from libreyolo import LibreYOLO

dfine = LibreYOLO("LibreDFINEl.pt")      # 31.24M params, 60.0 mAP@50-95
rtdetr = LibreYOLO("LibreRTDETRr50m.pt") # 36.59M params, 53.8 mAP@50-95

results = dfine("image.jpg")
